entries.title: Jeremiah 4:2
segments: Shalt swear, The Lord liveth; swearing by Jehovah's name, when it is performed in sincerity, is an open profession of allegiance to him in opposition to all false gods.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:3
segments: Break up your fallow ground; the hearts of the Jews are compared to untilled ground, covered with thorns, and unfit to receive good seed.
To break it up, is to put away their obduracy and their abominations.  Compare

, "Make you a new heart and a new spirit." 
 
True reformation must begin with an inward preparation of the heart to receive and obey God's word; that obedience which is only outward and forced is short-lived, and generally ends in making a man's last worse than the first.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:4
segments: Circumcise yourselves to the Lord; circumcision was the outward sign of consecration to God.  The Jews are here exhorted to do that inwardly which the outward rite signified.
No outward rite has, in and of itself, any saving efficacy.  The inward grace of which it is the sign can alone bring men into a state of salvation.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:5
segments:
Declare ye; the approaching invasion of the Chaldeans. 
 
  Into the defenced cities; for protection against the invaders.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:6
segments: Toward Zion; calling the people to flee to it as their strong-hold.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:7
segments:
The lion; the Babylonian conqueror. 
 
Wicked kings and nations are under the control of God's providence, and he makes them at his pleasure the ministers of his purposes towards his people, whether of wrath or mercy.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:9
segments: When God forsakes a nation for its sins, its wisdom and strength fail, and it becomes an easy prey to its enemies.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:10
segments: Thou hast deceived this people; allowed them to be deceived by false prophets.  This was a judgment sent upon them by God for loving falsehood rather than truth.  Compare

. 
 
The most dreadful judgment upon a people is, that God should give them up to the delusions of false teachers, who flatter them in sin, and promise them peace in the way of transgression.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:11
segments:
Of the high places; coming over the barren hills.  The reference is to the hot and withering wind from the eastern deserts. 
 
vv 11-31. 
 
The terrible desolations which God brought upon Judah and Jerusalem for their rebellion against him, are a perpetual warning to nations who enjoy the light of Christianity, of the calamities which will overtake them as they depart from him.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:12
segments: Unto me; unto Jehovah, that is, for the execution of his vengeance.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:13
segments: He shall come; the Chaldean monarch.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:15
segments:
From Dan; a city in the northern extremity of the land. 
 
  Mount Ephraim; the mountainous region of Ephraim also lay toward the north, through which the invader would approach Jerusalem.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:16
segments: Watchers; that is, besiegers, as the following verse explains.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:17
segments: Keepers of a field; persons set to guard it against robbers and beasts.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:19
segments: My bowels; the bowels are the seat of compassion.  See note on
.  In this and the two following verses Zion is the speaker, or the prophet personating Zion.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:22
segments: For my people is foolish, they have not known me; in this verse God speaks.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:23
segments: I beheld; the prophet has a vision of the utter desolation of the land.  The description is borrowed from that of the primitive chaos.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:24
segments: Moved lightly; quivered under God's wrath.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:29
segments:
The whole city; rather, as the same words are rendered just below, "every city," that is, of Judea. 
 
  They shall go into thickets; the Jews shall go for shelter.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:30
segments:
Rentest thy face; rather, "thine eyes," by applying a black paint to the eyelids.  This is done by passing an instrument smeared with the paint along the lids.  Judah is here compared to a harlot, who, in her eagerness to apply the paint, tears or furrows the lids. 
 
  Thy lovers; the idolatrous allies to whom the Jews looked for help against the Chaldeans.
